---
title: "Running a Bioconductor mirror"
date: 2026-09-30
---

This replaces the rsync-over-SSH instructions at
`bioconductor.org/about/mirrors/mirror-how-to/`. Those instructions depend on
`master.bioconductor.org`, which [milestone M2](roadmap.qmd) retires. The
new site has no rsync server. Instead it publishes a **manifest**: a list of every object in
the package repositories, with sizes and MD5s, that any HTTP client can sync from.

**No credentials, no sign-up form, no SSH key.** Fetch the manifest, fetch the files, recreate
the symlinks, serve the tree.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read this before running any sync command
`packages/release/` and `packages/devel/` are **not directories on the new site**. They are
symlinks resolved per request, and object storage has no symlinks. A sync scoped to
`packages/release/` sees an empty listing, not an error. With `rclone sync` or
`aws s3 sync --delete`, an empty remote means **your entire existing mirror is deleted to
match it.** Always sync from the manifest, always `copy` rather than `sync`, and always
dry-run first and check the object count.
:::

## What changed

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Source | `bioc-rsync@master.bioconductor.org` over SSH | `https://bioconductor.org/api/v1/manifest/index.json` over HTTPS |
| Access | SSH key, requested by form | none |
| Tool | `rsync -zrtlv --delete` | `rclone copy --files-from` |
| Symlinks | created by hand: `release` and `devel` | listed in the manifest index (202 on 2026-09-30); the script recreates `release`, `devel` and the R-version aliases |
| Current version numbers | in the rsync module names | in `index.json`, read every run |
| Cadence | release monthly-ish, devel at most weekly | manifest regenerated on every hourly sync; syncing daily is enough |

## The manifest

| Endpoint | Contents |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/manifest/index.json` | which numeric versions `release` and `devel` point at, the symlink map, per-manifest object counts, generation timestamp |
| `GET /api/v1/manifest/<version>/<repo>.tsv.gz` | `path` · `size` · `md5`, one object per line, tab-separated |

Repos are `bioc`, `data-annotation`, `data-experiment`, `workflows` and `books`, for the
current release and devel only. Older releases are not published; ask if you need them
([reporting a problem](report.qmd)).

The MD5 is a real MD5 of the object, not a composite ETag. An empty third column means no
usable hash exists for that object and it should be checked by size alone. Today that column
is populated for every object.

## Choosing scope

Decide explicitly rather than mirroring everything.

| Scope | Notes |
|---|---|
| `bioc` (`src/contrib`, `bin/windows`, `bin/macosx/*`) | Every mirror needs source. Binaries are comparable in size; skip if your users build from source. |
| `data-annotation`, `data-experiment` | Large, changes rarely. |
| `workflows`, `books` | Small. |
| Releases before the current one | Not in the manifest. |
| The historical archive (4.66 TB) | Not in the manifest. Never carried by any mirror. |

Release and devel together are roughly 320 GB.

## Running the sync

[`mirror-sync.sh`](mirror-sync.sh) is a short wrapper around `rclone copy`. It needs `bash`,
`curl`, `gunzip`, `jq` and [`rclone`](https://rclone.org/install/), and checks for them before
doing anything. It runs on Linux and macOS (`brew install jq rclone`).

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://seandavi.github.io/bioc-infrastructure/mirror-sync.sh
chmod +x mirror-sync.sh
DEST=/srv/bioc ./mirror-sync.sh          # DEST is the directory you serve as the site root
```

From cron, daily is plenty:

```sh
17 3 * * *  DEST=/srv/bioc /usr/local/bin/mirror-sync.sh >> /var/log/bioc-mirror-sync.log 2>&1
```

### What it does

1. **Reads `index.json`** for the current release and devel versions, every run. Nothing is
   pinned: at a release roll the script follows the new numbers by itself.
2. **Lists every file** in those versions' manifests for the repos you carry, then applies
   your `INCLUDE`/`EXCLUDE` patterns. A failed manifest download stops the run.
3. **Copies with `rclone copy --files-from`.** Only new and changed files are fetched, judged
   by size and modification time. rclone writes each file under a temporary name and renames
   it when complete, so your server never serves a half-written file. rclone doesn't check
   the manifest's MD5s; they're there if you want to verify a copy yourself.
4. **Recreates the symlinks** (`release`, `devel` and the R-version aliases inside
   `contrib/`). rclone can't make them, and without them, URLs that go through them
   return 404 on your mirror.

**It never deletes.** rclone's http backend can't list directories on this site, so
`rclone sync` can't tell "removed upstream" from "not listed" (see the warning above).
Old package versions stay on disk until you remove them. At a release roll, delete the
retired version yourself, e.g. `rm -rf /srv/bioc/packages/3.22`.
That also clears the older tarballs that piled up while it was current.

### Settings

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `DEST` | (required) | Directory you serve as the site root. |
| `REPOS` | `bioc data-annotation data-experiment workflows books` | Which repositories to carry (see [Choosing scope](#choosing-scope)). |
| `INCLUDE` | everything | Extended regex; copy only paths that match. |
| `EXCLUDE` | nothing | Extended regex; skip paths that match. |
| `RCLONE_*` | | Any rclone setting, e.g. `RCLONE_TRANSFERS=16` for more parallel downloads. |

Patterns match the full path, e.g. `packages/3.23/bioc/src/contrib/limma_3.66.0.tar.gz`.
Source packages only, no data repos:

```sh
DEST=/srv/bioc REPOS="bioc workflows books" INCLUDE='/src/contrib/' ./mirror-sync.sh
```

Exit status is `0` when done, and non-zero with a message on stderr otherwise. A failed run
has deleted nothing; rerun it.

### Without the script

The script is the recipe; you can run its steps by hand or adapt them. The part that
matters is the file list:

```sh
curl -fsS https://bioconductor.org/api/v1/manifest/3.23/bioc.tsv.gz | gunzip | cut -f1 \
  | grep '/src/contrib/' > files.txt
test -s files.txt
rclone copy --http-url https://bioconductor.org :http: /srv/bioc --files-from files.txt --no-traverse
```

A bare `rclone sync` against a directory URL, the way `rsync` used to work, isn't possible
yet: the site serves no directory listings for rclone to read. That's tracked in
[bioc-edge#61](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/61).

## Serving

Apache and nginx serve the tree as-is. Two things to get right:

- **Follow symlinks.** Apache needs `Options +FollowSymLinks` on the directory, or every
  `release/` URL returns 403.
- **Do not copy `.htaccess` from the old origin.** It redirects old-release traffic out to
  the archive, which would send your users away from your own mirror.

Content types come from your server's `mime.types`, so extensionless files such as
`PACKAGES` and `VIEWS` behave as they always have.

Users point at your mirror exactly as before:

```r
options(BioC_mirror = "https://mirror.example.org")
BiocManager::install("GEOquery")
```


## Migrating an existing rsync mirror

Point the script at the `DEST` you already serve and run it by hand the first time. rsync
kept the old origin's timestamps, which differ from the new site's, so the first run may
download much of the tree again; later runs fetch only what changed. If `packages/release` or
`packages/devel` is a real directory rather than a symlink, move it aside first, or the
script's link lands inside it. Nothing is deleted, so files the old tree has that the manifest
doesn't stay until you remove them. Tell the Bioconductor team when you have switched, through the
[site problem form](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/new?template=site-problem.yml), so the rsync
account can be closed on your say-so rather than on log silence.

## Listing your mirror

The mirrors page and `chooseBioCmirror()` are still the registry. That process has not
changed; the request form on the [mirrors page](https://www.bioconductor.org/about/mirrors/)
still applies.

## Source

The generator and the reasoning behind the design, including why read-only storage
credentials and a custom client were rejected, live in the serving repo's `MIRRORS.md`.
